football_evidence.question: Can Louisville’s pass rush get to Davis Warren?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.9 points.
supporting: When Stanford has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Stanford’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 17.3% of its runs, and Louisville’s defense stops 11.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Stanford’s offensive line No. 48 nationally and Louisville’s No. 132.
contradicting: When Louisville has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Louisville’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.9% of its dropbacks, and Stanford’s defense sacks the quarterback on 1.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When Louisville has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Louisville’s offense averages 7.3 yards per carry, and Stanford’s defense allows 5.9 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Louisville has the ball (the red zone): Louisville’s offense succeeds on 51.8% of its red-zone plays, and Stanford’s defense allows success on 58.9% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).

When Louisville has the ball (big plays through the air): Louisville’s offense turns 16.2% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Stanford’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).
quarterbacks: Lincoln Kienholz has completed 122 of 182 passes (67.0%) for 1,848 yards, 10.2 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in seven games for Louisville, and has been sacked on 14 of 196 dropbacks.
Davis Warren has completed 163 of 272 passes (59.9%) for 1,933 yards, 7.1 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in eight games for Stanford, and has been sacked on 12 of 284 dropbacks.
